theses.intro: Four signs would show the money behind AI data centres running short. Each is marked from KKReckons stories, and changes only when the evidence does.

conditions.label: Funding on harder terms
conditions.test: An AI-infrastructure borrower can't refinance, or pays sharply more to borrow.
conditions.evidence: Yields on CoreWeave's 2031 notes passed 16% and its five-year default insurance hit a record 1,194.5 basis points on 15 October. No one has forecast a default; it reports results in November.

conditions.label: A hyperscaler cuts capex
conditions.test: Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon or Meta lowers its AI spending plans.
conditions.evidence: None has lowered its spending plans. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report results this week.

conditions.label: Chip and GPU rental prices fall
conditions.test: The price of renting AI chips, or of the memory they use, turns down.
conditions.evidence: No fall reported. CME plans futures on H100 and B200 rental prices, which would give this a public price to watch.

conditions.label: Banks can't offload AI loans
conditions.test: Lenders are left holding data-centre debt they meant to sell on.
conditions.evidence: Banks are still trying: a group including JPMorgan and MUFG has spent over six months placing $38bn of Oracle-leased project debt, and some lenders will sell at a discount.
